result.title: CompositionEvidence: Controlling Geometric Evidence for Cinematic Composition Reasoning with Frozen Vision-Language Models
result.comment: Accepted at the 33rd International Conference on MultiMedia Modeling (MMM 2027)
result.summary: Cinematic composition questions depend on in-frame geometry that vision-language models (VLMs) use inconsistently. External perception tools can expose this geometry, but naive prompt injection can overwrite useful visual predictions. On ShotBench composition, pre-question geometry reduces Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 49.5% to 46.3%; corrupted measurements lower it to 33.6%. CompositionEvidence derives nine reproducible features from frozen detection, depth, and line experts and supplies their shared 24-dimensional representation through two interfaces. A training-free channel appends gated neutral evidence after the question, reaching 56.2% (+6.7, exact McNemar p=0.0018) and 48.4% under corrupted evidence. A minimal-training channel maps the same representation to four soft tokens with a 7.37M-parameter projector while leaving the VLM frozen; it reaches 61.0% (+11.5). Across nine VLMs, including five commercial models queried through official provider APIs, zero-shot accuracy ranges from 43.8% to 63.0%, and the text channel changes it by +6.7 to -6.9 points; the highest baseline is among the regressions. The effect of explicit geometry depends on measurement reliability and on how the receiving model integrates it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究冻结VLM如何利用电影构图所需的帧内几何证据：从检测、深度、线段专家中提取九个可复现特征及共享24维表示，通过免训练的文本门控通道与7.37M参数投影器映射为四个soft token两种接口注入，在ShotBench及九种VLM上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接给出「外部视觉证据注入会覆盖原有视觉预测」以及效果取决于测量可靠性与接收模型整合方式的诊断，与LVR关注的视觉旁路、证据筛选和soft token式latent接口密切相关，可供核查其门控与表示共享的实际作用。
